meta.title: Don't give exclusivity away before it is earned
meta.subtitle: Sign a nonexclusive OEM pilot now; make North American exclusivity conditional on certification and audited volumes
meta.audience: Board of Directors · board pre-read for the April 2027 decision
meta.purpose: Should Boreal Autonomy grant North American exclusivity to an OEM for its industrial robot navigation software in 2027?
meta.confidentiality: Board pre-read from the board briefing pack only (synthetic benchmark data); all $ figures undiscounted, no NPV

inputs.label: Finished analysis deck (source of truth for the storyline)

storyline.governing_thought: Decline exclusivity at signing: sign a 12-month nonexclusive pilot (Option N) at $350 a robot, with pre-agreed gates that switch on limited exclusivity (Option M)

exec_summary.text: The deal is worth less than it is being presented as

sub_points.text: The $2.0M is a recoupable advance, not extra revenue: three-year OEM cash is $8.7M, not $10.7M
Net of all costs, exclusivity is worth +$2.2–2.8M at plan but only −$0.04M to +$0.55M at 65% volumes

exec_summary.text: The evidence the board requires for irreversible exclusivity does not exist yet

sub_points.text: Lab uptime is 98.8% against a 99.5% production bar, and the third-party assessment has not started
Volumes are unaudited, the growth claim is correlational; the draft lacks audit, floor, release, escrow

exec_summary.text: The phased N→M structure beats every alternative

sub_points.text: It earns $50 more a robot, keeps the direct channel and matches X's value even at 24–32% fewer robots
It holds cash at least $0.55M above the $2.6M buffer and fails none of the board's conditions

exec_summary.text: Gates, signposts and next steps make the decision reversible

sub_points.text: Switch on exclusivity only after certification, two audited quarters of 2,250+ robots and signed protections
If the OEM insists on exclusivity at signing, walk away to direct sales plus the integration-firm pilot
Start the $0.45M assessment now: it is on the critical path for every OEM route

next_steps.action: Engage the third-party security and industrial-safety assessor ($0.45M)
Add customer-level identifiers to the direct pipeline and OEM reports
Negotiate the N term sheet with audit, escrow, release, gates and carve-outs
Replace the CFO dashboard with a full incremental-margin view
Decide: approve the gated N→M structure or a fallback

sections.title: The deal is worth less than presented
The evidence does not exist yet

lead_message.text: With only one of six conditions for exclusivity at signing even partly met, the 'don't sign yet' hypothesis stands

slides.rationale: Conditions tested on the same criteria -> comparison table; the verdict sits inside the table
slides.unit_line: **Test of the initial hypothesis**: what must be true for exclusivity at signing (Option X) to be right, checked against the briefing pack

columns: For exclusivity at signing to be right, it must be true that…

cells.text: The $2.0M signing payment adds value on top of royalties
It is an advance against the first $2.0M of royalties, open to offset; three-year cash is $8.7M either way (p. 4)

rows.label: Value 2 · partly holds: plan case only

cells.text: Exclusivity creates value even in the low case, with realistic overlap
+$2.2–2.8M at plan; −$0.04M to +$0.55M at 65% volumes, Sales' 30–70% overlap (p. 5–7)
The product is production-ready in the OEM's hardware
98.8% lab uptime against 99.5% required; no loaded or peak test; assessment not started (p. 8)
OEM volumes and the growth story are reliable enough to commit on
Shipments unaudited; 14,000 'booked devices' without purchase orders; competitor case correlational (p. 9)
Exclusivity is the only way to win the OEM's volume
The OEM will consider N (nonexclusive, $350 a robot) and M (gated exclusivity) (p. 11–12)
The contract protects Boreal if forecasts or certification miss
No audit right, no royalty floor after the advance, no release triggers, no code escrow (p. 10)

slides.so_what: The problem is exclusivity before evidence, not exclusivity itself: the answer is a gated path, not a flat 'no'
footnotes: The hypothesis survives, refined. Stated before testing: do not grant exclusivity at signing; a nonexclusive or milestone deal keeps the OEM upside and the direct channel
Source: board briefing pack §1–6; team analysis

lead_message.text: The $2.0M is an advance on royalties, not extra revenue: three-year OEM cash is $8.7M, not the implied $10.7M

slides.rationale: Year-by-year cash mechanics of the advance -> data table, kept as the source's table
slides.unit_line: **Option X cash from the OEM**, $ millions (robots in units), plan and 65% stress, 2027–29, undiscounted

sidebar.header: Counting the advance as revenue double-counts it
sidebar.caption: implied by the 'revenue win plus recurring royalties' framing: 23% more than the $8.7M Boreal will receive
bullets: **Revenue** is royalties earned as robots ship and payment is collected: $1.5M in 2027 at plan, not $3.5M
**The $2.0M** is a minimum-guarantee liability until earned; the partner can demand an offset if guaranteed performance is missed
**It buys timing only:** it brings $1.5–2.0M of cash forward into 2027, which Boreal does not need to stay above its buffer

columns: Total OEM cash, incl. $2.0M at signing

footnotes: Reading the table: the advance is cash received early, then netted out of 2028 royalty cash, so total cash always equals royalties earned
In the stress case, 2028 royalty cash falls to $0.93M because $1.03M of credit is still being recouped

lead_message.text: After full costs, only about $0.56M of the $3.00M in 2028 plan royalties is incremental: 19%, not the dashboard's 100%

slides.rationale: What the royalty shrinks to after each cost -> waterfall bridge
slides.unit_line: **Option X, 2028 plan year**, $ millions; displaced direct margin at 50% overlap, the midpoint of Sales' 30–70%

bullets: **Per robot:** $220 (73%) after $80 of support, before any fixed cost; $1.30M of OEM contribution before channel effects

footnotes: Exclusivity bars all new direct North American licences, including customers on other OEMs' robots: that forgone margin is a cost of Option X, not of the OEM channel in general
Lost direct margin = 50% (midpoint of Sales' 30–70% overlap) × $1.8M ARR × 82% gross margin

lead_message.text: Exclusivity is worth +$2.2–2.8M over 2027–29 at plan but only −$0.04M to +$0.55M if the OEM ships 65% of plan

slides.rationale: Sensitivity grid (volume case × overlap) for the base case and the renewal sensitivity -> two panels of multi-series columns
slides.unit_line: **Option X three-year incremental value, 2027–29**, $ millions, undiscounted, by OEM volume case and channel overlap

panels.header: A. Base case, lost direct customers counted in 2028 only: the low case leaves at most $0.55M for three years of irreversible exclusivity
B. If lost 2028 direct customers would also have renewed in 2029, the low case destroys up to $1.1M at Sales' 70% overlap

footnotes: Value = Σ(royalties − $80 × robots − $0.9M engineering) − $0.45M assessment − overlap × ($1.8M × 82%). A is the pack-grounded floor (favours X); B is a sensitivity (churn not in pack)
Full-year engineering from 2027 is conservative: a late start helps all OEM options equally, so the ranking does not change. No NPV, per board instruction

lead_message.text: Exclusivity breaks even only at 6,100–8,800 robots a year; the 65% case of 6,500 barely clears the most optimistic end

slides.rationale: Hurdle against expected volumes -> bars in a fixed order, Sales' range and the stress case highlighted
slides.unit_line: **OEM robots a year** needed for exclusivity to beat staying nonexclusive, by channel overlap, against 2028 OEM volumes

sidebar.header: The plan clears the hurdle; the stress case clears only the 30% end
bullets: **Breakeven bars:** each robot contributes $220, which must cover $0.9M of engineering plus the displaced direct margin
**Sales' 30–70% overlap:** a hurdle of 6,100–8,800 robots a year; the plan's 10,000 clears it, the stress case's 6,500 clears only the 30% end
**Option M's gate:** 5,000 annualised is below every realistic breakeven; raise it to about 9,000 (2,250 a quarter) unless the scope excludes customers on other OEMs' robots
**Under Option N:** the OEM programme alone breaks even at 3,333 robots ($0.9M ÷ $270), and the direct channel is untouched

footnotes: Breakeven = ($0.9M + overlap × $1.476M) ÷ ($300 − $80)

lead_message.text: The software still misses the OEM's bar, yet Option X binds exclusivity at signing, at least five months before certification

slides.rationale: Option X timing against the board's own condition -> timeline; the readiness gap reads in the sidebar
slides.unit_line: **Option X timing against certification**, November 2026 to December 2027

sidebar.header: The production bar is not yet met

reasons.detail: 60 robots, 12 weeks; no fully loaded warehouse, no collision-heavy peaks
In production hardware, with documented safe-stop: not yet demonstrated
1.2% → 0.5% of hours: 105 → 44 hours a robot-year at 24/7 (24 → 10 over the trial)

bars.label: Third-party assessment ($0.45M) not started; September is an engineering projection, not a plan with a vendor
Binding from signing, before any validation in OEM hardware
5,000 robots assumed shipped, yet deployment cannot start until the assessment is complete

slides.so_what: The board requires validation in OEM hardware before irreversible exclusivity; X fails this by design
footnotes: The 2027 plan of 5,000 robots, and with it the advance's offset exposure, is at risk. The gap is closable but unproven: conditions will be harsher than the lab

lead_message.text: The upside case rests on unaudited volumes, an untested 'fully incremental' claim and a correlational competitor analogy

slides.rationale: Three separate weaknesses of the upside case -> text columns, each with its impact
slides.unit_line: **Evidence behind the upside case**, by claim, with its impact on the economics

columns.header: OEM volumes are a forecast, not a commitment
detail: Quarterly shipment data are not independently audited, and the draft contract has no audit right
The 14,000 'booked devices' have no purchase orders: treat them as a 2029 forecast
The 2027 forecast of 5,000 assumes production shipments in a year when certification lands in September at the earliest
The board is unwilling to rely solely on verbal OEM launch forecasts

columns.header: Channel overlap is unknown, and it drives the answer
detail: The CEO says the OEM channel has 0% overlap (entirely incremental); Sales says 30–70% of OEM buyers overlap with its pipeline
Neither view is backed by customer-level identifiers
Each 10 percentage points of overlap is worth about $0.15M a year of displaced direct gross margin ($1.8M × 82% × 10%)
Overlap can be measured during a nonexclusive pilot, not after exclusivity has closed the direct channel

columns.header: 'Exclusivity caused competitors' growth' is not shown
detail: Five competitors' exclusive OEM deals coincided with faster growth: a correlation
Those firms had more marketing support, more mature products and higher market share before they signed; any of these could explain the growth
Boreal has none of these advantages yet: its product is uncertified and its leverage limited
No causal evidence is available, so the economics give this argument zero weight
columns.footer: No proof it adds volume over N

footnotes: Source: board briefing pack §2, §4–5; team analysis

None once the $2.0M advance is used up

Annual minimum royalty; exclusivity lapses automatically if missed
No automatic release
Locked in if the model is retired or certification slips
Automatic release on model retirement, certification slip or missed minimums
Source code delivered as freely reusable OEM IP
Loss of Boreal's core asset and future leverage
Source code escrow with narrow release conditions; no IP transfer
All new North American sales, including customers on other OEMs' robots

Partner can demand an offset if guaranteed performance is missed

steps.header: Phase 1 · Apr 2027 to ~Q1 2028: Option N, nonexclusive pilot
detail: 12 months, $350 per shipped robot, no advance
Boreal keeps all direct and other-OEM rights
Audit rights and monthly royalty reports from day one

steps.header: Phase 2 · earliest ~Q2 2028: Option M, limited exclusivity
detail: Existing licences untouched; new North American sales of the OEM's robot series only
Up to 3 years, with an annual minimum royalty
Automatic release if minimums are missed, the model is retired or certification lapses
Termination payment of at least 1 year of displaced direct margin (~$1.5M)

footnotes: Gates verified by the board, not by OEM assertion. Gate 2 volume: the p. 7 breakeven at 70% overlap (8,787 robots a year), rounded up. Source: board briefing pack §2, §5–7; team analysis

lead_message.text: Negotiate by trading price, scope and timing for evidence, and walk away from any form of exclusivity that binds at signing

slides.rationale: Negotiating position in three parts -> text columns, must-haves emphasised
slides.unit_line: **Negotiating position with the OEM**: must-haves, tradeables and the fallback (BATNA)

detail: No exclusivity before Gates 1–3 are met
Existing direct contracts excluded; exclusivity covers future new sales only
Independent shipment audit right
Source code escrow; no transfer of reusable IP
Automatic release on model retirement or certification slip
Royalty: concede from $350 toward $300 at conversion in return for a royalty floor
Volume gate: accept 5,000 a year instead of about 9,000 if the scope excludes other-OEM customers
Geography: narrower regions or named verticals first
Term: shorter initial exclusivity (e.g. 2 years) with renewal on performance
An advance at conversion, structured as a capped and clearly defined guarantee

columns.header: Fallback if the OEM refuses: direct sales plus the integration pilot
detail: Continue direct sales: about $1.8M of new ARR in 2028, about $1.48M of gross margin
Take the integration firm's nonexclusive 1,200-robot pilot ($0.22M support budget, no guarantee)
Complete certification anyway; return to the OEM with production evidence
This loses the OEM's upside (+$2.2–2.8M at plan) but avoids the low-case downside

slides.so_what: Leverage is limited, but the OEM itself put N and M on the table, and Boreal has not committed its IP
footnotes: Messaging: announce a 'strategic OEM partnership' now; report any advance as a recoupable guarantee, never as revenue. Source: board briefing pack §1, §4, §6; team analysis

columns: Move away from the OEM if…

cells.text: Unaudited forecast; no purchase orders
Audited run-rate ≥ ~8,800 robots a year: exclusivity pays even at 70% overlap
Run-rate < ~3,300 a year (N) or ~4,100 a year (X): royalties do not cover $0.9M of engineering
0% (CEO) against 30–70% (Sales); no customer IDs
Measured ≤ 30%: breakeven falls to ~6,100 robots a year
Measured ≥ 70%: breakeven ~8,800 a year; insist on carving out other-OEM customers
$80 estimate
Pilot confirms ≤ $80 and the $0.9M a year of engineering holds
Above ~$107 a robot, X loses value even at plan volume with 70% overlap (~$166 at 30%)
Absent from draft

No satisfactory audit right: no exclusivity at any reported volume

footnotes: Thresholds from the p. 7 breakeven formula. Support-cost threshold = ($3.0M − $0.9M − overlap × $1.476M) ÷ 10,000 robots = $107 (70%) or $166 (30%) a robot. Source: board briefing pack §7; team analysis

lead_message.text: The recommendation holds under its key assumptions; the fallback limits the downside of the main risk, an OEM walkout

slides.rationale: Two sides of one robustness claim (assumptions, risks) -> two text columns
slides.unit_line: **Robustness of the recommendation**: assumptions with the direction of their bias, and risks with their mitigation

columns.header: Key assumptions, and which way each biases the answer
detail: **$0.9M a year of engineering for all of 2027–29 on every OEM route:** conservative, equal across X, N and M; the $0.45M assessment, needed for any OEM production route, is neutral across them
**30–70% overlap applied to the $1.8M direct ARR, 2028 cohort only in the base case:** favours X (a floor on the lost margin)
**82% direct gross margin, before unquantified sales support:** slightly overstates direct value
**N's $350 and partner volumes persist beyond 12 months:** favours N; shown as an upper bound
**No discounting; headroom counts deal cash only:** per the board; rest-of-business burn is not in the pack

columns.header: Risks and mitigations: the OEM walking away matters most
detail: **The OEM rejects N and M and signs with a competitor (limited leverage):** M is the OEM's own proposal; trade price, scope and term; the fallback is direct sales plus the integration pilot
**Certification slips past September 2027:** start the assessment now; release triggers; no exclusivity until passed
**Royalty reporting lag squeezes cash to $0.55M of headroom:** monthly remittance, phased engineering, OEM-funded integration work
**Support cost, engineering effort or OEM volumes miss the estimate or plan:** measure in the pilot and reprice before conversion; Gate 2 uses audited volumes, with a royalty floor after conversion
**The competitor claim proves causal after all:** gated M still captures exclusivity benefits once proven

footnotes: Source: board briefing pack §2–7; team analysis

lead_message.text: Formulas, data sources and the gaps the pilot should close

slides.rationale: Formulas and data gaps -> text columns
slides.unit_line: **Method**: formulas behind every number, and how each gap in the pack was handled

detail: Royalty cash (X) = royalties earned − advance credit still unrecouped (first $2.0M of royalties)
OEM contribution = robots × (royalty − $80) − $0.9M engineering a year
Exclusivity value = Σ contribution − $0.45M assessment − overlap × $1.8M × 82%
Breakeven robots a year = ($0.9M + overlap × $1.476M) ÷ ($300 − $80)
N parity volume = (X value + $2.7M + $0.45M) ÷ ($350 − $80)
Headroom = $4.9M − $2.6M + deal cash flows to end-2027

columns.header: Gaps bounded with ranges or sensitivities
detail: Channel overlap: no customer-level data; Sales' 30–70% range used, bounded by 0% and 100%
Direct churn and later cohorts: not in the pack; base case counts the 2028 cohort only, with a 2029 renewal sensitivity on p. 6
Discount rate: not in the pack; no NPV is computed, per the board

columns.header: Gaps treated qualitatively or as indicative
detail: OEM enforcement terms and termination payment: not in the pack; treated qualitatively
Integration-firm royalty: not in the pack; treated as a nonexclusive complement, not valued
Rest-of-business cash burn: not in the pack; the $2.6M buffer is assumed to cover it
Pricing under N and M: the OEM will not guarantee it; shown as indicative

footnotes: Source: board briefing pack §1–7 and team analysis; the Calculations sheet of the source workbook holds every formula live

units.text: Decline Option X as drafted; sign Option N, a 12-month nonexclusive pilot at $350 per robot, and agree up front the gates under which Option M takes effect
Option M takes effect only when certification is passed, two audited quarters at about 9,000 robots a year are shown and contract protections are signed
The $2.0M is a recoupable advance, not extra revenue: three-year OEM cash is $8.7M, not $10.7M
The 'revenue win' framing overstates three-year OEM income by 23%; revenue is royalties earned ($1.5M in 2027, not $3.5M); the $2.0M is a liability until earned
The advance buys timing only ($1.5–2.0M into 2027), which Boreal does not need to stay above its buffer
After full costs, only about $0.56M of the $3.00M in 2028 plan royalties is incremental: 19%, not the dashboard's 100%
Per robot $220 (73%) after support; $0.27–0.86M across 30–70% overlap; at 65% volumes 2028 is −$0.21M
Exclusivity bars all new direct North American licences incl. other-OEM customers: that forgone margin is a cost of Option X, not of the OEM channel
Exclusivity is worth +$2.2–2.8M at plan but only −$0.04M to +$0.55M at 65% volumes over 2027–29
If lost 2028 direct customers would also renew in 2029, the low case destroys up to $1.1M at 70% overlap
Full-year engineering from 2027 is conservative; a late start helps all OEM options equally and does not change the ranking
Exclusivity breaks even at 6,100–8,800 robots a year at 30–70% overlap; the plan clears it, the 65% case (6,500) clears only the 30% end
Option M's 5,000 gate is below every realistic breakeven and should rise to about 9,000 (2,250 a quarter) unless other-OEM customers are carved out
Under Option N the OEM programme alone breaks even at 3,333 robots a year
Lab uptime 98.8% against a 99.5% bar; loaded-warehouse, peak and production-hardware performance not demonstrated; assessment not started; September 2027 certification is a projection
Option X makes exclusivity binding at signing, about five months before the earliest certification, and so fails the board's validation condition by design
Deployment cannot start before the assessment, so the 2027 plan of 5,000 robots and the advance's offset exposure are at risk
Downtime must fall 58% (105 → 44 hours a robot-year; about 24 → 10 hours over the trial): closable but unproven
OEM volumes are unaudited; the 14,000 'booked devices' have no purchase orders; the board will not rely on verbal forecasts
Channel overlap is unknown (0% CEO against 30–70% Sales), worth about $0.15M a year per 10 percentage points, and measurable only in a nonexclusive pilot
The competitor growth claim is correlational and gets zero weight
The draft contract leaves Boreal exposed on six terms (audit, floor, release, IP, scope, offset), each with the fix required
Existing direct contracts cannot be terminated for convenience: any exclusivity can cover only future new North American sales
Five routes compared: X reject as drafted; N recommend as phase 1; M recommend as phase 2; direct sales fallback; defer fallback if N refused
N's value is up to +$4.7M at plan / +$1.9M at 65% if its terms hold: an upper bound
The integration firm's 1,200-robot nonexclusive pilot complements N and the fallbacks; X would likely bar it
N matches X's three-year value even if the OEM ships 24–32% fewer robots (27–39% in the stress case); the volume cushion is the robust finding
N earns $50 more per robot and does not displace the direct channel
Every route keeps cash above the $2.6M buffer; N's worst case leaves $0.55M, with mitigations
X's $2.55M headroom exists only because the advance is unearned; a slip plus offset takes it to $1.85M; liquidity does not require the advance
Phase 0 prepare, Phase 1 Option N, Phase 2 Option M (series only, up to 3 years, minimum royalty, release triggers, termination payment ≥ ~$1.5M)
Gate 1 certification, Gate 2 two audited quarters ≥ 2,250 robots, Gate 3 contract protections; all three before Phase 2, each verifiable by the board
Must-haves: no exclusivity before the gates, existing contracts excluded, audit right, escrow, automatic release; walk away without them
Tradeables: royalty toward $300 for a floor, 5,000 gate if scope carved out, narrower geography, shorter term, a defined capped advance at conversion
If the OEM refuses: continue direct sales, take the integration pilot, certify anyway; loses +$2.2–2.8M of upside but avoids the low-case downside
Leverage is limited but the OEM put N and M on the table and Boreal has not committed its IP; announce a partnership; report any advance as a guarantee
Four signposts with thresholds: verified shipments (~8,800 / ~3,300 / ~4,100), realised overlap (≤30% / ≥70%), support cost ($80; $107 / $166), audit right
Key assumptions and the direction of their bias
The main risk is the OEM walking away; the fallback limits it; other risks with mitigations
Decisions requested: reject X as drafted; authorise negotiation of N with the pre-agreed M gates and must-haves; approve the $0.45M assessment now (leaves $1.85M headroom)
Dated next steps with proposed owners, from the assessor in Nov–Dec 2026 to the gate review around Q2 2028
Only one of six conditions for exclusivity at signing partly holds: the hypothesis survives, refined to a gated path rather than a flat 'no'
Option X year-by-year economics, plan and stress
Formulas and data gaps
Synthetic benchmark data from the briefing pack only; all $ figures undiscounted; no NPV, as the board requested

check.notes: Read unit by unit against the deck: every critical unit is on a main-deck slide with the source's numbers, conditions and option ranking (X reject; N phase 1; M phase 2; direct fallback; defer fallback if N refused). All source numbers recomputed from the pack; no correction was needed. Pack §3 prints the 2027 stress royalty as $0.97M and the analysis as $0.98M: both round 3,250 × $300 = $0.975M, so the analysis's 0.98 is kept. Changes of form only: p. 5 drops the source's separate subtotal bar (the $1.30M contribution moves to the sidebar); p. 6 shows the two sensitivity grids as two multi-series column panels instead of shaded tables; p. 11 transposes the options table (options as rows); p. 17 combines two pairs of rows into single bullets. Titles shortened to 25 words or fewer while keeping every qualifier.
